solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Game to enter gay movement: follow-up to a reckless tweet?

indicators.note: movement means shifting about, so these letters are moved into a new order
to enter is to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A sporting figure joins a gay rights march, then has to backtrack after an ill-judged post online.
explanation.walkthrough: The three rearranged letters become A-G-Y, and the game slips in after the A to give APOLOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: After posting something careless online, the usual next step is to say sorry publicly, so the definition describes it by its typical occasion.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) Feign ignorance about 'lady bump'

indicators.note: about can mean scattered around, so the letters are thrown into a fresh order

blocks.note: the quoted words supply the eight letters

explanation.surface: Someone pretends not to know anything about an awkward 'lady bump', a pregnancy rumour perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'lady bump' look like a phrase being discussed; they simply fence off the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend not to know something is an idiom for acting as though one cannot speak or understand.

clue.text: Who stands at the entrance, issuing stupid order, OK, about piss-up

indicators.note: something stupid is senseless, so the letters are jumbled into nonsense
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: both words taken as written, then rearranged
piss is slang for urine, pee

explanation.surface: A bouncer on the door barks a daft instruction while a drinking session gets going around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss-up' looks like a drinking session, but it splits into the slang word plus a reversal signal; the rearranged letters wrap round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A porter or gatekeeper is the person stationed at a door to admit or turn away visitors.

clue.text: One of ten with the Sun? Contemptible sort

blocks.note: we have ten toes
the Sun is a tabloid newspaper, and a rag is a low-quality paper

explanation.surface: A question about one of ten people connected with the Sun newspaper, followed by a verdict on them.
explanation.walkthrough: One of ten looks like a person on a team, but it is a digit of the foot. A toerag is British slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a worthless, despicable person, originally a rag wrapped round a tramp's feet.

clue.text: Taking top off, ups the temperature for members

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, and taking it off removes it

blocks.note: to raise the temperature of something is to heat it

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off their top makes things steamier for club members.
explanation.walkthrough: Members here are limbs of the body, not people in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Members is an old word for limbs or body parts, and the upper limbs are a common example.

clue.text: Who'd selfishly use whip's standard measure against presenter?

blocks.note: a standard is a flag or banner
an ell is an old measure of length
Ant McPartlin, of the TV presenting duo Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: A party whip deploys a standard procedure against a broadcaster for their own ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The whip looks like a parliamentary enforcer; it is the lash. Ant and Dec are a famous British TV presenting double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a person scourges their own body, often as religious penance, so the lash is used on oneself.

clue.text: Rank peer welcoming totally useless leaders

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only opening letters are kept
to welcome is to take in, so one piece receives another

blocks.note: to peer is to look hard, to stare
the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A lord of the realm opens the doors to hopeless figureheads, a sign of how bad things are.
explanation.walkthrough: Rank and peer look like nobility; peer is a verb meaning look, and rank means standing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words denote someone's standing or importance relative to others, a synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Possible contraceptive that hurts? Here's something for your head

blocks.note: the pill is an oral contraceptive
ow is what one cries when hurt

explanation.surface: A contraceptive that causes pain, and then someone offers a headache remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: Something for your head sounds like a painkiller; it is what you rest it on in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushion laid on a bed supports the sleeper's skull, so it is literally provided for that part of the body.

clue.text: Wretched bunch of Tory lords, lost without Duke

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken away
something lost has gone astray, so the letters wander into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for Duke

explanation.surface: A gloomy view of the Conservative peers in the Lords, adrift since a ducal member left.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the D from the nine letters, then rearrange the remaining eight.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitiful group of people is called a sorry lot in idiomatic English, sorry meaning miserable and lot meaning set.

clue.text: Deposit sexual partner on back

indicators.note: back means going backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: a lay is slang for a sexual partner
re means on, as in concerning

explanation.surface: Someone puts their lover down on their back.
explanation.walkthrough: Deposit reads as a verb; it is a noun, a sheet of sediment.
explanation.definitionFit: A deposit of sediment or rock laid down over time forms a stratum, which is the noun meant here.

clue.text: Anticipation of sore nuts being nursed by Barney

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled
to be nursed is to be held in the arms, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a barney is British slang for a row or fight

explanation.surface: Someone dreads their sore testicles being tended by a man called Barney.
explanation.walkthrough: Sore nuts reads as an injury; nuts is the anagram signal and Barney a British word for a quarrel, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to predict and plan for future events is the same as looking ahead, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Prior, or Cook, on the radio?

indicators.note: radio is heard not seen, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a fryer is one who cooks in fat

explanation.surface: A question about a radio show: is it Prior, or Cook, both possible surnames of broadcasters.
explanation.walkthrough: Prior and Cook look like surnames; one is a monastic office and the other a verb-turned-noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior heads a religious house, and in loose crossword usage any member of a mendicant order serves as an example.

clue.text: Coming to a conclusion, Boris & Co's party?

blocks.note: first meaning: inferring, as in 'I take it'
second meaning: the euphemism used for the Downing Street lockdown parties

explanation.surface: A dig at Boris Johnson's Partygate, as the inquiry reaches its verdict on his social events.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson's team insisted the lockdown parties in Downing Street were work events, the word in the answer being their chosen term.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduce something is a sense of the verb, and a social meeting of people is the noun, both one word.

clue.text: Want erotic stimulation, something for one's spirit maybe

indicators.note: stimulation stirs things up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: both words supply the ten letters

explanation.surface: Someone craving sexual excitement, which might lift their mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Spirit sounds like the soul; it is a distilled drink such as gin, which is commonly mixed with this.
explanation.definitionFit: This quinine mixer is added to gin or vodka, an example of something poured into a liquor.

clue.text: (& 24dn.) Beastly hunk, Pablo, messed around with rear

indicators.note: something messed around is jumbled up, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A brutish handsome man called Pablo fooled about with someone's backside.
explanation.walkthrough: Beastly reads as nasty and hunk as a sexy man; together they mean a huge animal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Arctic animal is a massive predator, so a great lump of a wild creature describes it playfully.

clue.text: Religious type in favour of match with a heartless fanatic

indicators.note: without a heart means losing the middle, so the central letter goes

blocks.note: pro means for
a Test is an international cricket match
taken as written
a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic

explanation.surface: A devout person who supports a game alongside a cold-hearted zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is a top-level international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Western churches that split from Rome at the Reformation is an example of a believer.

clue.text: Prat in liaison (dodgy) offering enlightenment

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

blocks.note: all three words supply the thirteen letters

explanation.surface: A fool in a shady affair claims to be bringing others wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed dodgy reads as an aside about the affair; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stirs the mind or gives fresh insight is uplifting, close to a synonym of giving illumination.

clue.text: Ready for bed, went to bed – er, backed off

indicators.note: backed means moved backwards, so the letters are reversed
off means removed, so letters are taken away

blocks.note: to retire is to go to bed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sleepy hesitates mid-sentence and then retreats, having gone to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'er' looks like a hesitation; it is two letters which, reversed, are stripped from the front of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sleepy and in need of rest is exactly the state of being prepared to sleep.

clue.text: Right leaning leader involved with OBE is accepted by Boris – for a sum

indicators.note: a leader comes first, so only the opening letter is kept
involved means tangled, so the letters are twisted into a new order
to be accepted is to be taken in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right
its first letter
taken as written
Boris Johnson was Prime Minister, PM

explanation.surface: A right-wing figure honoured with an OBE by Prime Minister Johnson, in exchange for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at honours for sale; 'for a sum' is the link and definition. An OBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sum in arithmetic is an exercise to be worked out, an example of a mathematical question.

clue.text: Cyclops' rest disturbed, ending in Jimmy Riddle

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters are moved
the ending of a word is its final letter, the one kept

blocks.note: Cyclops is the setter, so what is his is 'my'
taken as written, then rearranged
its final letter

explanation.surface: The setter's sleep is broken by the need for a wee.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, a wee; the phrase splits so that Riddle alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question or enigma, something unexplained, a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: About to get arsehole to take place again

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
a cur is a contemptible man, a swine

explanation.surface: Someone about to be landed with an obnoxious person turning up at a venue once more.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsehole is slang for a nasty person, here a scoundrel or mongrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that keep happening repeatedly are said to come round once more, a direct synonym.

clue.text: How power might be delivered at present

blocks.note: first meaning, read whimsically: by means of electric flow
second meaning: now

explanation.surface: A question about the way electricity reaches us these days.
explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is a jokey reading of the adverb as 'by current', the flow of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: Electricity travels as a flow of charge, and the ordinary adverb means now or in these times.

clue.text: They're mindful of Brenda boarding coaches

indicators.note: to board a vehicle is to get inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, ER
coaches are railway carriages, or cars

explanation.surface: People who keep an eye on Her Majesty as she gets onto the coaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called the late Queen Brenda, and ER (Elizabeth Regina) is her royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: People who look after the sick or elderly attend to them, so they are those who keep others in mind.

clue.text: Steps into sack being pissed

indicators.note: into means going inside, so one piece is put within another

blocks.note: a set of steps is a stepladder
the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles into bed while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed is British slang for drunk, not angry; the answer is equally British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang for heavily intoxicated, synonyms in that informal sense.

clue.text: see 2dn.

explanation.walkthrough: Norman Tebbit was a prominent minister under Margaret Thatcher. Drop one B and turn the rest round.

clue.text: see 14ac.
First Lady (Republican) wants encore, on and on without end

blocks.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
R is the abbreviation for Republican
an audience calling for an encore shouts 'more'

explanation.surface: A Republican President's wife wants an encore, and keeps demanding it endlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: First Lady looks like a president's wife; it is the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means always, for all future time, matching endless continuation.

clue.text: Kinky fun? Atmosphere not right

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into another order

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
the air is the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A bit of kinky fun, but the mood in the room feels wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Not right reads as a comment on the mood, but it is the definition, meaning unjust.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unjust or unequal in treatment is morally wrong, a direct synonym of the answer.
